name: OpenDDS
listed_description: An open source C++ implementation of the Object Management Group (OMG) Data Distribution Service (DDS).
reason: README and repo pages have no performance numbers or baseline. performance-tests/bench holds tooling only. Third-party DDS comparisons that name it (ros2 performance_test, i11eperf, Middleware 2023 and RTCSA 2023 systematic evaluations, seen as search snippets, the papers and the ROS discourse thread were blocked) rank OpenDDS behind Fast DDS and Cyclone DDS; i11eperf README has no results. No gRPC comparison found. No claim that it beats any baseline.

name: oSip
reason: gnu.org and antisip.com doc pages were egress blocked; search snippets show no speed claims. The only numeric context found is a Zebu parser paper (arXiv, snippet only) and a zero-copy SIP parser repo that use oSIP as the slower baseline, so oSIP is the comparison target, not the winner. No numeric claim of beating a baseline.

name: promise-cpp
listed_description: Header only library that implements Promise/A+ standard.
reason: Readme.md has no numbers or baseline; it only suggests using reject instead of throw and PROMISE_MULTITHREAD=0 'for better performance'. example/simple_benchmark_test.cpp and asio_benchmark_test.cpp print ns/op for its own switch loop with no comparison against std::future, libevent or asio callbacks, and no committed results. Author's README note says C++20 coroutines make the code obsolete.

name: Proxygen
listed_description: Facebook's collection of C++ HTTP libraries including an easy to use HTTP server.
reason: README and proxygen/httpserver have no benchmark numbers. The 2014 Facebook launch post (engineering.fb.com, blocked; seen via search snippet only) gives absolute echo-server throughput (up to 304,197 requests/s over SPDY 3.1, 32-core Xeon E5-2670) with no named baseline. A third-party HTTP/3 vs HTTP/2 study (arXiv, blocked, snippet only) uses Proxygen as a client, not as a winner. No numeric comparison against nginx, libcurl or any other baseline reached.
